projects.title: Network Automation Platform — UI Standardisation
projects.team: Product, architecture & engineering stakeholders across Australia, Finland, USA and France
kpis: One consistent UI across 5 operations applications
Light and dark themes from a single set of design tokens
Shared, reusable component library and UI standards
Designers and developers mentored on the system
projects.summary: Set the UX and front-end direction for a multi-application network automation platform covering assurance, performance and security. Owned the design system — design tokens, reusable components and UI standards — and applied it across five operations applications — including workflow management, scheduling, and procedure (MOP) launch and monitoring — with light/dark theme support.
projects.plainTerms: Telecom operators run their networks through several separate tools. Each one had grown its own look and behaviour, so people switching between them had to relearn the screens. I built one shared 'kit of parts' (a design system) — the same colours, buttons, tables and layouts — so all five tools now look and work alike. A 'MOP' (Method of Procedure) is a step-by-step instruction for a network change; two of the tools launch and track them, and a single switch flips them between light and dark mode. 'Design tokens' are simply named settings like 'primary colour' or 'standard spacing' that every tool reads from, so a change made once shows up everywhere.

projects.title: Field Operations Mobility App
projects.team: Product, engineering and QA teams with global stakeholders
kpis: Front-end delivered through to UAT closure
Cockpit screens that surface only what needs action
Change coordination and field-operations workflows covered
projects.summary: Designed and built dashboards and cockpit screens for change coordination and field-operations workflows, and led front-end delivery of the mobility application through to UAT closure.
projects.plainTerms: Engineers in the field and coordinators in the office need to know which network changes are planned, running or stuck. I designed 'cockpit' screens — one place that shows only the items needing attention, instead of long lists of everything. 'UAT' (User Acceptance Testing) is the final check where the customer's own users try the app and sign off that it does what they need; 'UAT closure' means they signed it off.

projects.title: Low-Code Integration Platform
projects.team: Product, architecture & engineering stakeholders across four countries
projects.timeline: 2024 – Present (Phase I live, Phase II in progress)
kpis: Phase I live in production
Phase II — a low-code application — in progress
Interaction patterns for automated, in-review and approved actions with human override
projects.summary: Delivered Phase I of an integration platform for network operations and now lead Phase II, a modular low-code application. Defined interaction patterns for AI-assisted operations with clear states for automated, in-review and approved actions, and a human override at every step.
projects.plainTerms: 'Low-code' means users build or adjust a workflow by arranging ready-made blocks on screen instead of writing program code. Parts of the work are suggested or carried out by automation and AI, so the screens always show whether an action was done automatically, is waiting for someone to review it, or has been approved — and a person can step in and override it at any time. That is what 'human-in-the-loop' means: the machine helps, but a human stays in charge.

projects.title: Operations Portal Framework Upgrade
projects.team: Engineering team with product and security stakeholders
kpis: Portal moved to a current Angular version
Known security vulnerabilities remediated
projects.summary: Led the Angular framework upgrade of the platform's operations portal, combined with remediation of security vulnerabilities in the front-end code and its dependencies.
projects.plainTerms: Angular is the toolkit the portal's screens are built with. Like phone software, it needs regular updates — older versions stop getting security fixes. I led the move to a current version and fixed the security weaknesses ('vulnerabilities') found in the code and the third-party libraries it relies on, so the portal stays safe and supported.

projects.title: AI-Assisted Development Adoption
kpis: AI coding assistants introduced to the team
Hands-on mentoring for designers and developers
projects.summary: Introduced AI coding assistants — GitHub Copilot, Cursor, v0 and Bolt — to the design and front-end team, with mentoring on how to use them in day-to-day UI work.
projects.plainTerms: These are AI tools that help write code. Copilot and Cursor suggest code as a developer types; v0 and Bolt can turn a written description or a sketch into a first working screen. I brought them into the team and coached people on using them well, so the team can turn ideas into working screens with AI help — with a person still reviewing what ships.

projects.title: Enterprise Intranet Portal & In-house Tools
kpis: Intranet portal and niche apps for 2,500+ users, delivered on schedule
90% less effort for effort booking and cost recharge (Time Tracking Tool)
CTO Business Excellence Award for a GUI-based automation tool
2× Appreciate Excellence Award; Nokia Quality Award 2013 nominee
projects.summary: Took the Nokia intranet portal and a pack of niche in-house applications from concept to delivery for 2,500+ users, planned the India global delivery centre rollout and extended delivery to other global centres. Also designed the time tracking, performance management and survey applications and a GUI-based automation tool.
projects.plainTerms: An intranet is a company's private website for its own staff. I designed and built it, along with everyday tools people used inside the company — for logging work hours, running performance reviews and running surveys. The time tracking tool cut the effort of recording hours and billing them to the right budget by 90%. A 'GUI-based automation tool' lets people automate repetitive tasks by clicking through screens instead of writing scripts.

projects.title: Alarm Triage Copilot
kpis: Clickable prototype covering triage to approval
AI suggestion shows evidence and confidence, never acts alone
Test plan for 5 NOC engineers
projects.summary: A clickable prototype of an AI copilot for a network operations centre. It groups related alarms, suggests a likely root cause with evidence, and asks a person to approve each next step.
projects.plainTerms: When something breaks in a network, dozens of alarms fire at once. This concept shows how an AI assistant could point to the probable cause and propose fixes, while an engineer stays in control and approves every action. A "prototype" is a clickable mock-up used to test an idea before anything is built.

projects.title: Offline Site Survey App
kpis: Works fully offline; syncs when signal returns
Large touch targets for gloved hands
GPS and time tagged on every photo
projects.summary: A mobile prototype for field engineers surveying cell sites with poor signal: checklists, photo capture and a clear offline-to-sync story.
projects.plainTerms: Engineers often visit remote sites with no mobile data. This app saves everything on the phone first and uploads it later, so no work is lost. The screens make it obvious what is saved, what is waiting to upload and what has synced.

projects.title: Network Change Approval — UX Flow
kpis: Future-state flow across four roles
Journey map from request to verification
Pain points turned into design opportunities
projects.summary: A swimlane flow and journey map for approving planned network changes — who does what, where decisions happen, and where automation can remove waiting.
projects.plainTerms: Before designing screens, it helps to map the whole process. This flow shows every step of approving a network change, split by who is responsible, and highlights where people wait or get stuck. A "journey map" adds what people think and feel at each step.

projects.title: Low-Code Builder — Onboarding Flow
kpis: First working flow in four steps
Every empty screen offers a next step
Same patterns in light and dark themes
projects.summary: A first-run experience for a low-code automation builder: pick a goal, start from a template, connect a source and see a safe first run — plus a set of helpful empty states.
projects.plainTerms: "Onboarding" is what new users see the first time they open a product. The aim here is to get someone to a working result in minutes without reading documentation. "Empty states" are the screens shown before there is any data — they should explain what belongs there and how to start.

projects.title: Design System Documentation Site
kpis: Live component previews with code and props
Light and dark themes from shared tokens
Responsive down to mobile
projects.summary: A documentation website for an operations design system: guidance, live component previews, code snippets and props tables in one place.
projects.plainTerms: A design system only works if teams can find and understand it. This website is the "manual" — it shows each building block, when to use it, and the code developers copy into their apps.

projects.title: This Portfolio Website
kpis: Designed and built end to end
Light and dark themes, responsive to mobile
Working contact form with spam protection
projects.summary: The site you are on: designed and built with React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, with a data-driven content model, light and dark themes and a PHP contact endpoint.
projects.plainTerms: Everything here — layout, colours, content structure and code — was designed and built by me. Content lives in simple data files, so projects can be added without touching the page code.

projects.title: Web Template Gallery & Mini Sites
kpis: Hundreds of mini sites, landing pages and templates
Logos and banners for a commercial template gallery
projects.summary: Early-career web design: mini sites, landing pages, web templates, logos and banners for a commercial template gallery.
projects.plainTerms: Before working on large software products I designed ready-made website templates that small businesses could buy and customise. It built the foundation for layout, typography and visual craft.
